Breaking: AI Completes the Largest Mathematical Proof in Human History, Mathematician Bursts into Tears on the Spot | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto News监管政策Breaking: AI Completes the Lar...Breaking: AI Completes the Largest Mathematical Proof in Human History, Mathematician Bursts into Tears on the SpotmarsbitPublished on 2026-10-30Last updated on 2026-10-30AbstractThe Classification of Finite Simple Groups (CFSG), the largest mathematical proof in history, has been fully formalized and verified by AI. Spanning roughly 15,000 pages and developed by about 100 mathematicians over more than half a century, the "Enormous Theorem" provides a complete "periodic table" of all finite simple groups: cyclic groups of prime order, alternating groups, the 16 infinite families of Lie type groups, and 26 exceptional sporadic groups—the largest being the Monster Group. Because the proof was so vast and scattered, it was notoriously difficult for any human to verify in full, and errors were nearly inevitable.

The startup Axiom used a multi-agent AI system, AxiomProver, to translate the entire proof into Lean code. Starting on October 1, 2026, the system completed the task in just 24 days, producing a 43.1 million-line Lean codebase—now the largest open-source software project by line count, surpassing the Linux kernel, Chromium, Firefox, LLVM, GCC, and FFmpeg. Along the way, the AI flagged hundreds of anomalies, including 34 significant logical gaps. Most notably, it found a fatal flaw in John Walter's 1986 proof of the Unbalanced Group Theorem, providing the counterexample PSL2(49). Working with group theorists Richard Lyons and Ronald Solomon, the team devised a new route, and the AI itself proved a new result, "Preservation of simple tops," to patch the gap. Previously, chat and coding had separate allowances; now both draw from a single shared pool, and usage will be measured in tokens rather than message counts. Only Instant chat remains unlimited. Users can check remaining quota and reset times under Settings → Usage, and when exhausted they can wait for a reset, upgrade, or buy credits. OpenAI has not specified an exact launch date or token amounts per tier.

The change follows a month of frequent quota resets and Codex updates led by Tibo (Thibault Sottiaux), who ran a 28-day challenge of daily improvements or full resets. During that period OpenAI doubled quotas for Pro 100/200/500 and Business Premium, but not Plus, drawing complaints. Tibo's remark about graduating from "The Reset Company" to "The Token Company" now looks like a preview of the pooled, token-based model.

Separately, OpenAI tightened device limits: a single device can use only a limited number of paid accounts across Go, Plus, and Pro tiers, with excess logins showing "Device limit reached" or being logged out. This undercuts users who rotated multiple subscriptions, just as multi-account switching arrived on mobile. Community reaction has been negative, with some Plus users saying they may buy more Claude instead, since independent chat quota was a key attraction. BofA's Hartnett: The Contradiction Between AI and ABB Is Detonating, and the Real Relief Window for Tech Stocks Won't Come Until Next Year | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto NewsMarket AnalysisBofA's Hartnett: The Contradic...BofA's Hartnett: The Contradiction Between AI and ABB Is Detonating, and the Real Relief Window for Tech Stocks Won't Come Until Next YearmarsbitPublished on 2026-10-30Last updated on 2026-10-30AbstractBank of America's Michael Hartnett warns that the collision between AI hyperscaler capex and bond market stress is pressuring the tech bull market. Hyperscaler debt issuance has surged to $182B in 2026 from $17B in 2024, while free cash flow is projected to swing from $240B in 2024 to -$180B by 2027 as capex rises to $1.2T. US IG tech bond total returns versus the broader IG index sit at a 30-year low, making tech credit "diamonds in the rough" with yields of 6-8% for mega-caps and 9-14% for some high-yield names. The "ABB" (Anything but Bonds) supertrend is itself pushing yields higher, disciplining the AI capex boom. While YCC/QE threats may cap disorderly yield rises, a real relief rally for risk assets and AI stocks likely requires lower yields and easier financial conditions—most plausibly in H1 2027 via geopolitical peace, falling oil prices, and an end to the hiking cycle. Global equities saw $566B inflows this week, with China equities taking in $257B, the largest since April 2025; Japan drew $68B, Europe saw $23B outflows, and gold had its first outflow since July 2026. The Bull & Bear Indicator eased to 7.1 (neutral). Democrats-sweep risk is being priced, though a 53-seat Senate win and a bond yield spike are not fully discounted. YTD, commodities lead at +91.6% (WTI +79%), US equities +14%, global equities +9.6%, while government bonds fell 3.3% and gold dropped 7.1%.#2027 Relief Window#ABB Trend#AI Debt#Bond Yields#China Equities#Fund Flows#Gold Outflows#Hyperscaler Capex#Rate Hikes#Tech BondsAuthor: Bu Shuqing, Wall Street Insights

Real-time news, insights, prices, trending stories, and expert analysis - all in one place.Singapore Blockchain Week 2026 Returns This November, Puts Singapore and Johor, Malaysia Cross-Border Digital Economy Opportunities in the SpotlightSingapore Blockchain Week (SBW) 2026 will take place from 13 to 17 November 2026 as a government-supported flagship event bringing together regulators, financial institutions, sovereign entities, family offices, founders, investors, enterprises, and ecosystem builders. The event features prominent speakers including H.E. Justin Sun (TRON), Jose Fernandez da Ponte (Stellar Development Foundation), representatives from VISA, J.P. Morgan, SAP, the United Nations Development Programme, Société Générale-Forge, Paxos, World Bank, and others.

SBW 2026 is positioned as the world's first cross-border blockchain week, connecting Singapore and Malaysia's Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) to accelerate innovation, investment, and technology collaboration across Southeast Asia. It is supported by partners including Singapore Global Network – Economic Development Board, Singapore Tourism Board, Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation, Iskandar Regional Development Authority, and Johor Corporation.

The week-long programme includes: Special Economic Zone Immersion (13 Nov), Tech-Enabled Sports (14 Nov), Learnathon (15 Nov), Inner Circle (16 Nov), and Institution Summit (17 Nov). The event focuses on the convergence of AI, DeFi, Real World Assets (RWA), and Venture Capital, positioning Singapore and ASEAN at the forefront of global digital transformation.

Nick Ducoff, General Manager of Institutional at Solana Foundation, recently highlighted the importance of invisible technology for crypto adoption. According to his tweet, the seamless integration of fast finality and low costs is what enhances the consumer experience. This perspective is crucial as the industry aims to bridge the gap between complex crypto solutions and everyday users, making it more accessible for the masses. You can view the original tweet here.

The Latest
The broader cryptocurrency landscape continues to show mixed signals, with various assets experiencing fluctuations that contribute to shifting market sentiment. In this context, Ducoff’s insights into Solana’s technological advancements come at a pivotal time. His emphasis on low-cost transactions and rapid processing aligns with current trends that prioritize efficiency and user-friendliness in blockchain applications. Institutions are increasingly focusing on how these features can attract a wider audience, potentially leading to a surge in adoption and usage.

Solana Foundation aims to enhance the blockchain experience by making technology more user-friendly and accessible. As a significant player in the crypto space, it focuses on innovations that facilitate smooth transactions and lower costs. The foundation’s efforts are essential as they align with the industry’s goal of mass adoption, particularly among non-technical users who may find existing solutions daunting.
